transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because my sleep is really broken up. I get off my overnight shift and just lie there awake, and when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up scared. It feels like I never get any rest at all.
When you wake up feeling scared, do you remember having a vivid, frightening dream, or do you just suddenly wake up frightened without recalling any dream?
I don’t really remember a dream. I just wake up scared, and then I can’t settle back down.
On your days off, when you're not working the overnight shift, do you still have this same trouble falling asleep and waking up scared, or does your sleep improve then?
It’s still bad on my days off. I’ll lie there awake for a long time, and if I do fall asleep, I wake up scared. I don’t feel rested either way.
How long have you been experiencing this pattern of difficulty falling asleep and waking up scared—days, weeks, or months?
About a year and two months now. It started after my agency switched me to rotating overnight shifts and added extra paperwork.

Aside from these nighttime awakenings, do you ever have sudden episodes of intense fear, rapid heartbeat, or feeling like you can't breathe during the daytime while you're awake and going about your activities?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I haven’t really noticed anything like that during the day.
Has anyone else—like a partner or roommate—ever seen you during these episodes, and if so, did they mention you screaming, thrashing around, or seeming confused and hard to wake?
I don’t have anyone there when it happens. I just know I wake up scared, and then I can’t really get back to sleep.
During the day, do you find yourself worrying excessively about work, finances, health, or other everyday things, even when there's no clear reason to worry?
I mean, I have things on my mind sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying all day for no reason.
Before your agency switched you to rotating overnight shifts, did you sleep well and wake up rested, or were you already having trouble sleeping before that schedule change?
Before the overnight shifts, I slept a lot better. Since the schedule changed, I get home and just lie awake, and when I finally fall asleep I keep waking up scared. I don’t feel rested at all.
Regardless of whether you're working or on a day off, do you find yourself feeling excessively drowsy or even accidentally falling asleep during your normal waking hours?
I’m tired, but it’s more that I can’t sleep when I get home. Then when I do finally fall asleep, I keep waking up scared, so I never feel rested.
When you wake up feeling scared, do you notice physical signs like your heart pounding, sweating, or shortness of breath, or is it mainly just a feeling of fear without those physical sensations?
It’s mainly just fear. I wake up scared, and then I can’t really settle back down. My sleep’s all broken up, so I never feel rested.
Over the past year, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
Yeah. Most days I wake up feeling heavy and empty. I used to go to church, do Zumba, help out with the kids at the center... but I just don’t feel like that person anymore.
Have you been feeling this down and uninterested in things nearly every day, for most of the day, for at least two weeks in a row—including on days you're not working?
Yeah. It’s pretty much every day, even when I’m not working. I wake up feeling heavy and empty, and I just don’t have interest in the things I used to do.

Besides feeling down and losing interest in things, have you noticed changes in your appetite or weight, trouble concentrating, feelings of guilt or worthlessness, or any thoughts about death or not wanting to be here?
I keep going over every little thing I’ve ever done wrong with patients or my family. It makes me feel like I’m a worthless aide... like God is mad at me because I didn’t protect people better.
Have you had any thoughts of death, or thoughts of hurting yourself or not wanting to be alive?
Yeah... I think about dying a lot, especially when I’m driving home in the morning. I just wish I could disappear, or not wake up, like everybody would be safer without me.
Did you start feeling this down, empty, and uninterested in things around the same time your sleep problems began, or did the low mood start separately, before or after the sleep issues?

I think it started around the same time. I came in because my sleep is all broken up now—after my overnight shift I just lie awake, and when I finally do sleep, I wake up scared and feel like I never rested at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a discrete, ~14-month period of depressed mood most of the day nearly every day, marked anhedonia (loss of interest in church, Zumba, volunteering), pervasive fatigue/insomnia not attributable solely to shift work (persists on days off), feelings of worthlessness and excessive guilt with religious overtones, and passive but recurrent suicidal ideation ('wish I could disappear, not wake up').
